in_sanskrit.name: धर्ति
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: One who holds, supports, or upholds. Derived from the root 'dhr' which means 'to hold'.

in_hindi.name: धर्ती
in_hindi.long_meaning: The Sanskrit word 'धर्ति' (dharti) translates to 'earth' or 'ground' in Hindi. The name 'Dhruti' can be interpreted as one who provides firmness, steadfastness, or support, similar to the earth beneath our feet.

in_tamil.name: திருத்தி
in_tamil.long_meaning: The Tamil translation of 'Dhruti' can be 'thiruththi', which means 'one who is firm, unwavering, or steadfast'. Alternatively, it can be 'thirumppan', which means 'one who inspires courage or confidence in others'.

in_telugu.name: ధృధి
in_telugu.long_meaning: In Telugu, 'ధృధి' (dhRidi) can be translated to 'dhRidheeshvara', which means 'Lord of steadfastness or firmness'. This name is often used to invoke the qualities of strength, courage, and support.

in_marathi.name: Dhruti
in_marathi.meaning: हिंदू नाव म्हणजे Firm, steady, support
in_marathi.long_meaning: Dhruti हे एक हिंदू नाव आहे जे भारतीय संस्कृतीत खोल आध्यात्मिक महत्त्व ठेवते। Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘dhru’ which means ‘that which is firm, steady, or enduring’. In Hindu mythology, Dhruti represents the goddess of patience, endurance, and fortitude. She is often depicted as the wife of Bhagiratha, the king who prayed to bring the god Ganga to earth.

in_bengali.name: Dhruti

In Hindu mythology, Dhruti represents the goddess of patience, endurance, and fortitude. She is often depicted as the wife of Bhagiratha, the king who prayed to bring the god Ganga to earth.
